Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates automated software engineering by asking a model to produce patches that fix real GitHub issues in Python repositories, validated by running the project’s tests in a controlled harness. The Verified subset filters tasks to those confirmed solvable and reliably testable, making pass@1 performance more comparable across systems.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style issue-to-patch evaluation beyond Python to multiple programming languages and ecosystems. It tests whether models can read unfamiliar codebases, localize faults, and implement correct fixes that pass language-appropriate tests and tooling.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor), Attention (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, more contamination-resistant software engineering benchmark designed to be closer to industrial practice, spanning multiple languages and more diverse tasks. Models must generate correct patches under realistic repository and test constraints, often requiring deeper debugging and multi-file refactors.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic coding and troubleshooting in a live command-line environment, where the model can run commands, inspect outputs, edit files, and iterate. Success requires choosing effective investigative commands, interpreting logs, and applying fixes under resource and time constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Adaptive Error Correction (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: BrowseComp evaluates deep web-based information seeking, where a model must locate evidence across documents and synthesize a correct final answer. It emphasizes search strategy, source selection, and faithful grounding in retrieved material rather than only parametric recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)

Description: τ2-bench (Tau2-bench) measures how well an agent completes multi-turn, tool-using customer-support workflows while following domain policies (e.g., retail, airline, telecom). It probes robust tool invocation, policy adherence under pressure, and cooperative dialogue with a simulated user.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control, Empathy (minor)

Description: OSWorld benchmarks multimodal “computer use” on an operating-system-like desktop, requiring navigation of GUIs to complete tasks within a step budget. Agents must perceive UI state, plan action sequences (click/type/scroll), and recover from mistakes in interactive workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid reasoning benchmark based on abstract grid transformation puzzles where the model must infer a hidden rule from a few examples and apply it to a novel input. The semi-private/verified evaluation setting is intended to reduce overfitting and better measure generalization to new patterns.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor), Planning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence and strategy in a simulated business management setting (running a vending machine business over an extended period). Models must make sequential decisions about inventory, pricing, negotiation, and adaptation to changing conditions to maximize final balance.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas measures real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol, requiring models to discover, call, and chain tools across multiple servers to complete tasks. It stresses correct parameterization, error handling, and synthesis of results into accurate outputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agent performance on tasks representative of entry-level financial analyst workflows, such as analyzing statements, answering finance questions, and producing grounded, audit-friendly outputs. It emphasizes structured reasoning, numerical/financial domain knowledge application, and report-style communication.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity capabilities by having models identify and (in some tasks) discover vulnerabilities in real open-source projects under a standardized harness. It tests interpreting vulnerability descriptions, navigating codebases, and producing correct exploit-relevant or fix-relevant outputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench measures how well agents can manipulate complex spreadsheets and solve realistic spreadsheet tasks, typically requiring reading/writing cells, formulas, and formats. It probes multi-step procedural execution and verifying outputs against task specifications.

Cognitive Functions:
L1:

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of GPQA consisting of very challenging multiple-choice science questions designed to be “Google-proof.” It emphasizes deep scientific reasoning and careful discrimination among plausible distractors rather than shallow pattern matching.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

Description: MMMLU is the multilingual extension of MMLU, evaluating broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects and numerous languages. It tests whether models can understand non-English prompts and apply subject knowledge consistently across linguistic contexts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates factuality and grounding behaviors of language models across multiple factuality-related tasks and settings. It focuses on whether models produce statements consistent with provided evidence and avoid unsupported claims, enabling more granular analysis than a single QA set.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified is a factual question answering benchmark with verification procedures intended to reduce ambiguity and label noise. It emphasizes precise, unambiguous answers and penalizes hallucinated or overconfident incorrect responses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: Global PIQA evaluates practical commonsense reasoning across many languages and cultural contexts using non-parallel (not one-to-one translated) items. It tests whether models can select plausible solutions to everyday situations while handling multilingual variation robustly.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) tests long-context multi-round coreference and retrieval by inserting multiple similar “needle” interactions into long “haystacks” and asking the model to reproduce the correct referenced content. It stresses maintaining and retrieving the right details despite interference from many near-duplicates.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Episodic Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval measures well-specified professional knowledge work across many occupations, judging the quality of produced work products (e.g., slides, spreadsheets, plans) against expert baselines. It emphasizes end-to-end execution quality, formatting discipline, and meeting constraints typical of workplace deliverables.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates software engineering agents on realistic, often longer-horizon engineering tasks that resemble contract or “freelance” work on codebases. It emphasizes implementing features and fixes with higher-level task understanding and integration across files and components.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: Graphwalks evaluates whether models can follow and reason over graph-structured relationships described in text, often requiring multi-step traversal (e.g., BFS-like navigation) and correct retrieval of nodes/paths. It stresses resisting distractions from similar entities and maintaining a consistent internal traversal state.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Planning, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Toolathon evaluates general tool-use competence across diverse tool APIs and tasks, emphasizing correct selection, sequencing, and parameterization of tool calls to accomplish goals. It targets robust agent behavior in multi-step workflows with intermediate state management and error recovery.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)
